fact: The Mairie de Bangui, the capital, signed an agreement on 12 December 2025 with the Ivorian firm BMI-WFS to digitise the city's municipal revenue; no other commune is named.
BMI-WFS, a firm under Ivorian law, is to run the digital collection system; its vice-president projects revenue up by over 200 per cent, and the project includes hiring and training 200 young people.
The agreement to digitise Bangui's municipal revenue was signed on 12 December 2025 in the presence of the Minister of Territorial Administration and Decentralisation.

A city-centre trader told RFI that Bangui town hall still has no computerised file of taxpayers and that collectors issue paper receipts; the town hall's IT head said a taxpayer database was being built (December 2020).
Municipal agents began a door-to-door census of traders in central Bangui in late 2020 to build a taxpayer database with an individual sheet showing what each owes.
